explanation: We always want our patients to get better! An idea for change is simply a practical way to make nursing care smoother and help patients recover faster.

question: A student finds that a new turning schedule stops pressure ulcers. Where should they suggest that hospitals use this routine?

options.A: In the methodology section
options.B: In the recommendations section
options.C: In the raw data appendix
options.D: In the front matter title page

explanation: The recommendations part is where you speak directly to clinical staff: 'Here is what we found, and here is how you can use it in the ward!'

question: During which early stage of HIV do patients often experience flu-like symptoms and a high viral load?

options.A: AIDS stage
options.B: Acute HIV infection
options.C: Remission phase
options.D: Clinical latency

explanation: Right after exposure, the acute stage hits with lots of virus replication and mild flu-like signs. You're learning fast!

question: Why is little-by-little exposure to radiation dangerous for healthcare workers over time?

options.A: It makes the nurse feel dizzy immediately after entering the room
options.B: It can cause gradual tissue damage and cellular mutations over years
options.C: It weakens the bones within a few minutes of standing nearby
options.D: It instantly heats up the skin and causes severe third-degree burns

explanation: Radiation adds up in the body over your career. That's why wearing your lead shield every single time is so important.

question: What is the solid ball of cells called that forms a few days after fertilization?

options.A: Trophoblast
options.B: Zygote
options.C: Blastocyst
options.D: Morula

explanation: After rapid cell division, the early embryo forms a solid cluster of cells resembling a mulberry, which is called the morula. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which topical preparation is oil-based, greasy, and best suited for thick, dry, scaly skin lesions?

options.A: Aqueous solution
options.B: Gel
options.C: Ointment
options.D: Lotion

explanation: Ointments have a high oil content which creates a protective seal over the skin, locking in moisture and treating dry skin conditions effectively. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h3)

question: In rural Nigeria, what is a major indirect reason why mothers sometimes sadly lose their lives before reaching the hospital?

options.A: Delays in reaching a healthcare facility due to poor transport
options.B: Routine use of sterile delivery kits
options.C: Early booking for antenatal care services
options.D: Excessive consumption of local herbs

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles mean transport delays are a massive hurdle. Getting mums to the clinic on time can literally save a life.

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential so vital in HIV nursing care?

options.A: Confidentiality laws prevent laboratories from processing viral load tests
options.B: Fear of social stigma often stops patients from seeking care or taking medications openly
options.C: Hospital management disciplines nurses who share room numbers with doctors
options.D: Uninsured patients will not pay their pharmacy bills if names are known

explanation: Spot on! Stigma is a huge barrier. Protecting privacy helps patients feel safe to come back for care and stick with their treatment.

question: How does burning medical plastics in the open air harm the environment?

options.A: They release toxic pollutants like dioxins and heavy metals into the air
options.B: They cause immediate earthquakes by destabilizing the local soil
options.C: They freeze the surrounding groundwater and kill aquatic life
options.D: They increase the amount of fertile compost available for local farming

explanation: Correct! Improper burning sends dangerous chemical smoke into the air, polluting both the atmosphere and the surrounding land.

question: What is the most effective way for nurses to help eliminate the practice of gishiri cutting in rural communities?

options.A: Arresting anyone who admits to performing the procedure
options.B: Banning all traditional birth attendants from practicing medicine
options.C: Distributing surgical blades to make the cuts safer
options.D: Working with local leaders and educating community members

explanation: Community engagement and respectful education build trust and help change cultural norms more effectively than punishment alone. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h7)

question: What is the main job of a drug antagonist?

options.A: To block receptors and prevent activation
options.B: To speed up the breakdown of cellular waste
options.C: To mimic hormones and cause a strong response
options.D: To increase the rate of drug absorption

explanation: Think of an antagonist as a stubborn security guard standing in the doorway—it sits on the receptor so nothing else can trigger it.

question: Which topical preparation is best suited for treating thick, dry, and scaly skin lesions?

options.A: A watery lotion
options.B: An oil-based ointment
options.C: A fast-drying powder
options.D: An alcohol-based liquid

explanation: Ointments have a heavy oil base that traps moisture and softens hard, thick, scaly skin much better than water-based creams or lotions. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h4)

question: Which of these forms the foundation (Tier 1) of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Running community support groups for grief
options.B: Ensuring access to food, shelter, and basic safety
options.C: Providing specialized psychiatric medications
options.D: Conducting individual trauma counseling

explanation: Spot on! Tier 1 is all about basic human survival needs like food, water, and physical safety before we can tackle deeper emotional issues.

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

options.A: To justify closing down the nursing department permanently
options.B: To make sure every single nurse on duty receives a formal warning
options.C: So the corrective action actually fixes the real underlying problem
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration has zero funds left

explanation: You nailed it! Finding the root cause ensures we fix the actual issue—whether it's a lack of training or a shortage of supplies—rather than just guessing.

question: What physical sign is tested by tapping the facial nerve near the cheek to check for low calcium?

options.A: Trousseau's sign
options.B: Brudzinski's sign
options.C: Chvostek's sign
options.D: Homans' sign

explanation: A quick tap on the facial nerve causing the cheek or lip to twitch is a classic positive Chvostek's sign, pointing to low calcium!

question: Why is the nursing rule 'if it wasn't charted, it wasn't done' so important?

options.A: Courts rely on written records as proof of care
options.B: Patients can demand a refund for missing notes
options.C: Hospitals refuse to pay nurses for unwritten tasks
options.D: Doctors will repeat every task not found in text

explanation: That is correct! Legally, if you didn't write it down, the court assumes the care never happened, no matter how hard you worked.

question: What is a fomite in the context of infection control?

options.A: A specialized mask used for airborne disease isolation
options.B: A living insect that carries parasites to humans
options.C: An inanimate object that can transmit infectious agents
options.D: A chemical spray used to clean hospital floors

explanation: Fomites are non-living surfaces or objects like stethoscopes or tables that hold onto germs and pass them along. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h3)

question: Which management approach is most effective for retaining experienced clinical nurses?

options.A: Discouraging further education to keep staff on the ward
options.B: Providing a supportive work environment and clear career growth
options.C: Ignoring staff complaints to maintain strict discipline
options.D: Forcing nurses to work overtime without extra compensation

explanation: Nurses stay where they feel valued, supported, and given real opportunities to advance their careers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h7)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team (doctors, nurses, physiotherapists) so important for patients with advanced disseminated sclerosis?

options.A: Physicians are not permitted to manage neurological disorders alone
options.B: The disease affects many different physical, cognitive, and emotional functions
options.C: It eliminates the need for any ongoing medical drug therapy
options.D: Patients require daily surgical procedures to replace damaged nerves

explanation: Because MS touches movement, speech, mood, and daily living, it takes a whole team of specialists working together to give the patient the best quality of life.

question: What is the best first step if an electrical piece of emergency gear fails to turn on?

options.A: Throw the device out the window
options.B: Abandon resuscitation efforts entirely
options.C: Check the power source and cable connections
options.D: Wait for a biomedical engineer to arrive

explanation: Brilliant! Often, it's just a loose plug or unseated battery that you can fix in seconds. Always check the basics first! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T11#GNS321_U2_T11_h5)

question: A patient at home is alert and refuses a scheduled dressing change. What is your best first move as a nurse?

options.A: Perform the procedure anyway since the doctor ordered it
options.B: Abandon the patient immediately and end your home care contract
options.C: Explain the risks of refusing, write down the details, and notify the doctor
options.D: Ask family members to force the patient to accept the treatment

explanation: Well done! Patients have a right to refuse care. Your job is to make sure they understand the risks, document everything clearly, and keep the medical team updated.

question: Why is tracking the baby's heartbeat so crucial when a mum is feeling distressed?

options.A: It stops the mother from feeling painful contractions
options.B: It calculates the exact time of delivery automatically
options.C: It measures the exact amount of maternal adrenaline in the blood
options.D: Stress reduces uterine blood flow, which can compromise the baby

explanation: Because stress cuts down blood flow to the womb, keeping a close eye on the baby ensures they are getting enough oxygen.

question: A patient with a mild fever and routine vaccination needs visits a nearby facility staffed by community health workers. Which level of care is this?

options.A: Quaternary level of care
options.B: Tertiary level of care
options.C: Secondary level of care
options.D: Primary level of care

explanation: Spot on! Community clinics handling everyday things like immunizations and mild fevers are right at the primary care level.

question: What is the main job of the alveoli in the breast?

options.A: Storing fat to give the breast shape
options.B: Synthesizing and secreting milk
options.C: Producing oxytocin for uterine contractions
options.D: Transporting milk directly to the skin surface

explanation: Spot on! The alveoli are tiny sac-like structures lined with special cells that actually make and secrete milk. You've got this!

question: Why is it important to involve community members at every step of an advocacy project?

options.A: It prevents government officials from visiting the health center
options.B: It relieves the nurse from doing any paperwork or reporting
options.C: It ensures that the nurse receives financial compensation from villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership so the community sustains the change long-term

explanation: Spot on! When people help fix their own problems, they take pride in the results and keep the good work going long after the nurse leaves.

question: When do international disaster management agencies step in to help?

options.A: To enforce international laws regarding border control during a crisis
options.B: To support local authorities when a disaster overwhelms national resources
options.C: To manage domestic healthcare systems during routine operations
options.D: To replace local governments permanently after a major emergency

explanation: You've got this! International agencies only step in with extra hands and supplies when local teams are completely overwhelmed by a crisis. They are there to support, not take over!

question: Why is it so important to include frontline nurses when reviewing hospital policies?

options.A: To give nurses extra administrative work during their night shifts
options.B: To prevent doctors from having any say in patient care standards
options.C: To fulfill a legal requirement that nurses write all hospital laws
options.D: To ensure the rules are practical and work well in actual clinical settings

explanation: Since frontline nurses carry out the care every day, their practical input ensures new policies are realistic and safe at the bedside.

question: Why do surgeons pump carbon dioxide gas into the tummy during a laparoscopy?

options.A: To stimulate the patient's breathing rate
options.B: To create a working space and visualize organs clearly
options.C: To sterilize the surgical instruments automatically
options.D: To cool down the internal organs during the operation

explanation: Correct! The gas puffs up the tummy like a balloon, lifting the wall away from the organs so the surgeon has plenty of room to see and work safely.

question: Why must a hospital conduct manpower planning before hiring new nurses?

options.A: To match the number of available staff with patient care needs
options.B: To decide which brand of uniforms the nursing staff will wear
options.C: To reduce the basic monthly salary of existing nursing staff
options.D: To fulfill government rules without needing actual hospital data

explanation: Manpower planning is just figuring out how many hands we actually need on deck so we don't end up severely understaffed or wasting money.

question: Why do health teams rush to carry out mass immunization campaigns as soon as a new refugee camp opens?

options.A: To prevent rapid outbreaks of vaccine-preventable diseases in crowded spaces
options.B: To fulfill mandatory international tourism travel requirements
options.C: To permanently cure all existing chronic medical conditions
options.D: To replace the need for clean drinking water and sanitation

explanation: When children are packed closely together in a new camp setting, infectious diseases can spread like wildfire. Quick vaccinations stop epidemics before they start!

question: What are the bumpy, distinct sections seen on the mother's side of a delivered placenta called?

options.A: Cotyledons
options.B: Decidual cells
options.C: Spiral arteries
options.D: Chorionic villi

explanation: You'll see this often in the maternity ward! The maternal side of the placenta is divided into about 15 to 20 carved sections known as cotyledons.

question: Why must you be extra, extra careful when doing nail care for a patient with diabetes?

options.A: The soap used for soaking can cause immediate chemical burns
options.B: Diabetic nails grow much faster than normal nails
options.C: Diabetic patients are allergic to standard metal nail clippers
options.D: Nerve damage and poor circulation increase infection and ulcer risks

explanation: You've got this! Because diabetes can cause poor blood flow and nerve damage (neuropathy), even a tiny nick can easily turn into a dangerous, slow-healing ulcer.

question: Why do organ transplant patients need to take immunosuppressive drugs long-term?

options.A: To prevent high blood pressure after surgery
options.B: To stop the immune system from rejecting the new organ
options.C: To help the surgical wound heal much faster
options.D: To help the new organ pump its own blood

explanation: Immunosuppressants act like a quiet button for the immune system, keeping it calm so it doesn't recognize and destroy the precious new donor tissue.

question: What is the most important approach when counseling a client on a tight food budget?

options.A: Scolding them for wasting money on fast food
options.B: Providing a rigid meal plan that cannot be changed
options.C: Insisting they buy only organic imported foods
options.D: Practicing active listening without judgment

explanation: Exactly! Listening without judgment builds trust and helps you truly understand your client's financial reality.

question: Why do we perform Leopold's maneuvers when a pregnant woman is admitted?

options.A: To determine the fetal position and presentation
options.B: To measure the mother's blood pressure accurately
options.C: To check if the amniotic fluid is clear or meconium-stained
options.D: To measure the exact cervical dilation in centimeters

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers are just our hands-on way of feeling the mum's tummy to figure out how the baby is lying inside.

question: Which rheumatic condition happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints?

options.A: Gout
options.B: Osteoarthritis
options.C: Fibromyalgia
options.D: Rheumatoid arthritis

explanation: Gout occurs when excess uric acid forms needle-like crystals in the joints, triggering sudden and very painful flare-ups. Drinking plenty of water and watching diet helps!

question: Why do people with hyperthyroidism often lose weight even though they eat a lot?

options.A: The digestive tract rapidly destroys ingested nutrients before absorption.
options.B: The body's basal metabolic rate is running at an accelerated speed.
options.C: Patients purposefully restrict their food intake due to severe anxiety.
options.D: Excess thyroid hormones cause constant nausea and vomiting.

explanation: Correct! Extra thyroid hormones put the body's engine into overdrive, burning through calories so fast that weight drops despite a big appetite.

question: What is the main job of extra protein during pregnancy?

options.A: Regulating sudden shifts in blood pressure
options.B: Preventing common digestive discomforts
options.C: Building uterine, breast, and fetal tissues
options.D: Providing quick energy for the mother's brain

explanation: Nailed it! Protein acts like the primary building blocks for the baby's growth, plus the mum's changing uterus and breasts.

question: What triggers the baby's circulatory system to close its fetal blood shunts?

options.A: Putting eye ointment in
options.B: Changes in oxygen levels and clamping the cord
options.C: The vernix washing away
options.D: Brown fat kicking in

explanation: When the cord is clamped and the baby takes that first big breath, oxygen levels change in the chest, telling those temporary fetal shunts to close up.

question: Why is the newborn wrapped in a clean cloth right after birth?

options.A: To absorb excess amniotic fluid for testing
options.B: To protect the baby from bright room lights
options.C: To stimulate deep breathing reflexes
options.D: To prevent heat loss and hypothermia

explanation: Newborns lose body heat very quickly through evaporation and environmental exposure, making prompt drying and wrapping essential. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which of these is a great example of a short-term rehabilitation goal?

options.A: Moving back into a completely independent apartment
options.B: Driving a personal vehicle across the country
options.C: Securing a full-time job in the community
options.D: Learning to transfer safely from bed to wheelchair

explanation: Small steps lead to big victories! Moving safely from bed to chair is a vital foundational skill needed early on.

question: Where should a nurse immediately dispose of a used injection needle after drawing blood?

options.A: In an open plastic trash bin
options.B: In a paper envelope
options.C: In a puncture-proof safety box
options.D: On the patient's bedside table

explanation: Sharps boxes are specially designed to prevent accidental needle stick injuries to healthcare workers and cleaners. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why do we encourage skin-to-skin contact right after a normal delivery?

options.A: It completely prevents the mother from experiencing postpartum bleeding
options.B: It speeds up the surgical healing of an episiotomy wound
options.C: It acts as a permanent immunization against childhood illnesses
options.D: It helps regulate the newborn's body temperature and encourages breastfeeding

explanation: That's right! Mum's body heat keeps the baby warm, and it gets breastfeeding off to a great start.

question: Where do most microbes found in the air come from?

options.A: Chemical reactions between sunlight and vehicle exhaust
options.B: Purely from indoor sterile laboratory equipment
options.C: They multiply and live permanently in the upper atmosphere
options.D: Soil, water, plants, and human or animal activities

explanation: Correct! Microbes aren't actually born in the sky. They get swept up from the ground, water, or living things around us.

question: Why are accidental needlestick injuries so scary for healthcare workers?

options.A: They stop the worker from ever touching medical tools again
options.B: They instantly paralyze the hand
options.C: They instantly trigger severe allergies to latex
options.D: They can push infected blood straight into the nurse's bloodstream

explanation: A hollow needle often carries leftover blood from a patient. That's why safe disposal isn't just about the patient—it protects YOU too!

question: What is the single most important factor for emergency contraception to work successfully?

options.A: The time of day the client ate their last meal
options.B: The age and weight of the client receiving the pill
options.C: The brand name of the emergency contraceptive drug
options.D: The timing of administration after unprotected sex

explanation: Time is everything with emergency contraception! The sooner you take it after unprotected sex, the better it works. Don't leave it too late!

question: Who is considered an 'informal caregiver' in elderly care?

options.A: Trainee medical students completing clinical rotations
options.B: Unpaid family members and friends who provide daily support
options.C: Hospital volunteers who visit patients on weekends
options.D: Licensed nurses who work part-time in nursing homes

explanation: Informal caregivers are usually loving relatives or friends who look after an older adult at home without getting paid.

question: A patient with newly fitted dentures is struggling to eat regular hospital food. What diet modification should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: A salt-restricted diet to control blood pressure
options.B: A soft diet to ease chewing discomfort
options.C: A high-fiber diet to stimulate digestion
options.D: A clear liquid diet for complete bowel rest

explanation: New dentures often cause sore gums, making a soft diet necessary until the patient adjusts. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h2)

question: What happens right after sound waves make your eardrum vibrate?

options.A: Cerumen is pushed out of the external canal
options.B: The auricle changes shape to capture more sound
options.C: The Eustachian tube opens to release excess air
options.D: The auditory ossicles move and amplify the vibration

explanation: The three tiny bones (malleus, incus, stapes) spring into action, boosting the sound vibrations before passing them deeper into the ear.

question: What is the medical term for those sudden waves of intense body heat and flushing?

options.A: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.B: Peripheral neuropathy
options.C: Vasomotor symptoms
options.D: Genitourinary syndrome

explanation: Hot flashes and night sweats involve blood vessels dilating, which is why we call them vasomotor symptoms. Keep it up!

question: What is the safest way to move a heavy patient up in bed without hurting your back?

options.A: Twist your torso to shift the weight in a single smooth motion
options.B: Ask the patient to push with their legs while you lift alone
options.C: Bend sharply at the waist to pull the patient quickly
options.D: Use an overhead mechanical lift and get a second staff member

explanation: Spot on! Protect your back by using mechanical tools and asking a colleague for help. Nursing is teamwork!

question: A patient is asked to stand up from a chair, walk ten feet, turn around, and sit back down. What is this clinical observation called?

options.A: Pulmonary function trial
options.B: Cardiorespiratory stress exam
options.C: Get-Up-and-Go test
options.D: Neurological reflex screen

explanation: The Get-Up-and-Go test is a quick, practical way to evaluate a patient's balance, sit-to-stand transition, and walking stability. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h3)

question: How do multidisciplinary ward rounds help improve rational drug use?

options.A: They eliminate the need for keeping written patient medical records

options.C: Doctors, nurses, and pharmacists review drug necessity together to catch errors early
options.D: They allow nurses to bypass doctors and prescribe medications independently

explanation: Collaboration across disciplines brings different perspectives together, ensuring safer and more rational medication orders. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)

question: When does the nurse's role in bereavement support typically begin?

options.A: Immediately after the patient's death and during the family's grieving process
options.B: Only after the funeral service has concluded
options.C: Months before the patient is admitted to the hospital
options.D: When the insurance company clears the final medical bill

explanation: Bereavement support starts right after death with post-mortem care and continues through follow-up outreach to help survivors cope with their loss. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h8)

question: What causes the microfilariae to leave the skin sample and enter the liquid?

question: Why is it super important to write down a clear methodology in your research?

options.A: To allow other researchers to replicate the study
options.B: To hide any potential errors made during data collection
options.C: To increase the total word count of the document
options.D: To prove that the researcher spent a lot of money

explanation: Good science can be repeated! Clear methods mean other nurses can test the same idea to see if it works for their patients too.

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention when it comes to gender-based violence?

options.A: To treat physical injuries sustained during an attack
options.B: To prosecute offenders in a court of law
options.C: To provide emergency shelter after an assault
options.D: To stop violence before it ever occurs through education and awareness

question: What is the name of the special fund in Nigeria set up to directly support primary healthcare facilities?

options.A: Basic Health Care Provision Fund
options.B: Universal Health Infrastructure Grant
options.C: National Emergency Medical Reserve Fund
options.D: Federal Drug Procurement Account

question: What does asking a patient to smile and puff out their cheeks help evaluate?

options.A: Cranial nerve I
options.B: Cranial nerve II
options.C: Cranial nerve VII
options.D: Cranial nerve VIII

question: Why is it important for other researchers to be able to repeat (replicate) a study?

options.A: It ensures the original researchers make a lot of money
options.B: It proves the findings are dependable if others get similar results
options.C: It allows the hospital to fire extra nursing staff
options.D: It guarantees that no human errors ever occurred

explanation: Spot on! When different people follow the same steps and get similar results, we can trust the findings much more.

question: What exactly is a paralytic ileus?

options.A: Rapid twisting of the sigmoid colon
options.B: Severe infection of the appendix lining
options.C: Temporary stoppage of intestinal peristalsis after surgery
options.D: A permanent blockage caused by a large tumor

explanation: Sometimes the bowel goes to sleep after abdominal surgery and temporarily stops moving. It's a common post-op watch-out for nurses!

question: What is a common consequence of low government budgeting for the health sector?

options.A: Out-of-pocket patient payments completely disappear.
options.B: Hospitals have an excess of modern diagnostic tools.
options.C: Facilities suffer from broken equipment and empty drug shelves.
options.D: Rural clinics receive more funding than urban centers.

explanation: When a government underfunds healthcare, hospitals and clinics lack the money needed to buy basic supplies, repair machines, and keep pharmacies stocked. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the name of the mature, fluid-filled follicle ready for release?

options.A: Primordial follicle
options.B: Corpus albicans
options.C: Graafian follicle
options.D: Atretic follicle

explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, large, fluid-filled stage of follicular development that ruptures during ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h2)

question: What happens inside the eye when a person reads a book held close to their face?

options.A: The cornea changes its physical shape to bend light
options.B: The ciliary muscles relax and the lens flattens out
options.C: The suspensory ligaments tighten and stretch the lens
options.D: The ciliary muscles contract and the lens becomes rounder

explanation: Think of it like a camera lens zooming in: for near vision, the ciliary muscle contracts, which loosens the ligaments and lets the elastic lens bulge rounder. You're mastering this step by step!

question: Why are range-of-motion exercises so important for a stroke patient with limited movement?

options.A: To reverse the original brain damage caused by the stroke
options.B: To speed up the metabolic rate and prevent weight gain
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any walking aids
options.D: To prevent painful muscle contractures and joint deformities

explanation: Moving those joints keeps them flexible and stops tight muscles from locking up permanently. Great job!

question: A ward nurse needs to visually track a post-operative patient's temperature fluctuations every two hours over a full day. Which graph should the nurse choose?

options.A: Bar chart
options.B: Line graph
options.C: Nominal table
options.D: Pie chart

explanation: Line graphs are designed to show trends and changes in numerical measurements over continuous intervals like time. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h6)

question: What does the letter 'C' stand for in the ACHES warning mnemonic for combined hormonal contraceptives?

options.A: Cold sweats
options.B: Chest pain
options.C: Chronic cough
options.D: Cramping pain

question: Which of these is NOT a common reason why nurses resist clinical change?

options.A: Excitement about learning too many new computer systems at once
options.B: Skepticism because past projects failed
options.C: Fear of a heavier workload during busy shifts
options.D: Comfort with familiar, everyday routines

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of a pelvic infection after a procedure?

options.A: Foul-smelling or purulent vaginal discharge
options.B: Severe and worsening lower abdominal pain
options.C: Persistent fever and chills
options.D: Sudden development of normal morning appetite

explanation: Spot on! Wanting to eat normally is a sign of a happy, healing body. Fever, bad-smelling discharge, and terrible pain are the real warning signs to watch out for.

question: You notice a yellow infectious waste bag is overflowing on your treatment trolley. What should you do?

options.A: Leave the bag open until the end of the shift for the cleaning crew
options.B: Tie the bag securely and replace it with a new one without pressing the contents down
options.C: Press the waste down firmly with both hands to make room for more items

explanation: Never push down on a waste bag with your hands! Hidden needles or sharp bits can easily pierce the bag and give you a severe injury.

question: What is a major reason why many women still experience home deliveries in rural Nigeria?

options.D: A direct instruction from the federal government

question: What does the handy acronym IMRAD stand for in research writing?

options.A: Introduction, Management, Results, and Documentation

options.D: Information, Measurement, Reporting, and Analysis

question: Why must a nurse sort and classify healthcare waste right at the bedside?

options.A: It prevents hazardous items from mixing with safe trash and reducing risks.

options.C: It ensures that kitchen scraps are safely sterilized before recycling.
options.D: It helps the hospital save money on buying heavy-duty office paper.

explanation: Spot on! Sorting waste right away stops dangerous things like used needles from ending up in normal trash bags where they could easily prick and injure anyone handling them.

question: What common physical issue can mild dehydration often mimic in a psychiatric patient?

options.A: Rapid hair loss and brittle fingernails
options.B: Sudden weight gain and high blood pressure
options.C: Complete loss of the sense of hearing
options.D: Fatigue, confusion, and worsening anxiety

question: How often should you check a mother's vital signs while she is stabilizing after a postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: Every 30 seconds
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Only once before leaving
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Checking every 15 minutes lets you catch early signs of shock or ongoing bleeding before they become life-threatening.

question: A postpartum mum complains of calf pain and swelling in one leg. What serious condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Normal postpartum cramping
options.B: Severe breast engorgement
options.C: Uterine subinvolution
options.D: Deep vein thrombosis

question: Why do droplet precautions only require a standard mask within a short distance of the patient?

options.A: Large respiratory droplets are heavy and quickly fall to the ground
options.B: Healthy lungs naturally repel moisture droplets from outside
options.C: Coughing only produces germs that travel upwards
options.D: Droplet nuclei dissolve instantly upon touching room air

question: How does training hospital staff on equity and human rights improve everyday patient care?

options.A: It replaces the need for basic clinical nursing skills and drug administration

options.C: It eliminates all infectious diseases within the hospital wards

question: What is the main perk of using an arterial line in an intensive care unit?

options.A: Checking oxygen levels without using a finger probe

options.D: Continuous, beat-by-beat blood pressure measurement

question: What is the protective protein coat that surrounds the genetic material of a virus called?

options.A: Flagellum

question: Why is removing patient names and personal details (de-identifying) so important in chart review studies?

question: As a psychiatric nurse evaluating a patient's unusual symptom, what is the most important question to ask yourself?

question: Which chemical messenger relaxes blood vessels in the penis to start an erection?

options.A: Nitric oxide

question: Why does eating a fatty meal trigger severe pain in someone with gallstones?

question: Why is chemoprophylaxis sometimes prescribed to health workers or travelers entering high-risk areas?

question: How do proper referrals help make the best use of our healthcare system's resources?

question: Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, a serious memory problem linked to heavy drinking, is caused by a shortage of which nutrient?
